title: Essentials of Networking
subtitle: Guess the hidden networking terms -- spin for consonants, buy vowels

gradeLabels.f: F-RANK -- Back to the Patch Panel

puzzles.hint: A switch link technique that carries traffic from multiple logical segments over a single physical connection using dot one Q tags.
puzzles.explain: Trunk ports tag outbound frames with an 802.1Q header containing the VLAN ID and strip that tag on ingress. Access ports, by contrast, carry only a single untagged VLAN.

puzzles.hint: A switch feature that restricts which hardware addresses can connect on a given interface, with configurable violation responses.
puzzles.explain: When the learned or configured MAC limit is exceeded, the violation mode determines the response: protect (drop silently), restrict (drop and log), or shutdown (err-disable the interface).

puzzles.hint: A screening method that monitors active connection records and automatically permits return traffic without an explicit rule.
puzzles.explain: Unlike simple packet filters that evaluate each datagram in isolation, this approach maintains a session table so that replies to established flows are allowed without additional administrator-defined permits.

puzzles.hint: A network segment that sits between two screening devices and hosts publicly reachable services such as web, mail, and name resolution.
puzzles.explain: Placing public-facing servers in this isolated segment limits the blast radius of a compromise: an attacker who breaches a public server still faces an inner barrier before reaching private internal hosts.

puzzles.hint: A mapping technique that allows an entire private network to share a single routable IP by differentiating sessions with unique source numbers.
puzzles.explain: The router rewrites both the source IP and a unique source port number for each outbound session and maintains a translation table to correctly forward return traffic to the originating internal host.

puzzles.hint: An automatically assigned IPv6 prefix in the fe eighty range that is valid only on the directly attached segment and cannot be forwarded by a router.
puzzles.explain: Every IPv6-enabled interface generates one of these from the fe80::/10 prefix, typically using EUI-64 or a random interface ID. It is required for neighbor discovery and router solicitation even when no global prefix has been assigned.

puzzles.hint: An optical cabling type that uses a laser source and a very narrow core to achieve transmission distances exceeding one hundred kilometers.
puzzles.explain: The small core diameter (typically 9 micrometers) allows only one propagation path for light, virtually eliminating modal dispersion and making this medium the standard choice for long-haul backbone and carrier links.

puzzles.hint: A remote-access configuration in which only organization-bound destinations are encrypted and forwarded through the secure channel while all other browsing exits directly.
puzzles.explain: This reduces bandwidth load on the corporate gateway by sending only internal-destined traffic through the encrypted path. The tradeoff is that internet-bound traffic bypasses corporate security controls, which is why some organizations mandate full-tunnel policy instead.
